name: MERLIon CCS Challenge
description: This paper introduces the inaugural Multilingual Everyday Recordings- Language Identification on Code-Switched Child-Directed Speech (MERLIon CCS) Challenge, focused on developing robust language identification and language diarization systems that are reliable for non-standard, accented, spontaneous code-switched, child-directed speech collected via Zoom. Aligning closely with Interspeech 2023 theme, the main objectives of this inaugural challenge are to present a unique first-of-its-kind Zoom videocall dataset featuring English-Mandarin spontaneous code-switched child-directed speech, benchmark the current and novel language identification and language diarization systems in a code-switching scenario including extremely short utterances, and test the robustness of such systems under accented speech. The MERLIon CCS challenge features two task: language identification (Task 1) and language diarization (Task 2). Two tracks, open and closed, are available for each task, differing by the
typical_sota_score: Task 1 (language identification): ~80–95% accuracy; Task 2 (language diarization): DER ~10–25% (lower is better)
reputation: A challenge benchmark from Interspeech for code-switched child-directed speech, with niche but relevant adoption in speech and language identification research.
notes: Speech benchmark with open and closed tracks; includes extremely short utterances, accented speech, and code-switching, making it challenging and not directly comparable to standard LID datasets.
